page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: An ecosystem is a functional unit of the
biosphere in which the members of a
community interact among themselves and with
the surrounding environment, in relation to
steps.why: The phrase functional unit is what marks an ecosystem out from a community: a community is only the living members, while an ecosystem is those members working together with their surroundings.
common_mistakes: Defining an ecosystem as all the plants and animals of an area. That is a community.
Leaving out the surrounding environment. The non-living part belongs to the ecosystem.
steps.memory_tip: Community is the living members alone; ecosystem is those members plus their surroundings.
steps.margin_note: One sentence. It must contain both interact and surrounding environment.

steps.label: Parts and example
lines: An ecosystem has a living (biotic) part and
Ex: a lake, a pond, a forest.
steps.why: Splitting the ecosystem into its biotic and abiotic parts turns the definition into something that can be checked against an example, and a lake is an example that carries both parts.
common_mistakes: Giving only living things as the example. A named place such as a lake carries both parts.
Writing the words biotic and abiotic without saying what they mean.
steps.memory_tip: Two parts, two words: biotic is the living half, abiotic is the non-living half.
steps.margin_note: Name the two parts and give one example. Three lines are enough.

insider_note: A lake is the example to give, because one named place carries both the biotic and the abiotic part.
